CRITICAL fix (Expert): the Shabbat deploy-freeze failed OPEN (deployed during Shabbat if hebcal unreachable), contradicting the skill's stated purpose. Made it fail CLOSED in the inline action (curl ... || echo ""; if [ -z CANDLE ] -> frozen=true) and the canonical reference. Re-review caught that the reference's bare $(curl) aborted under bash -eo pipefail before the fail-closed branch; fixed with CURL_OK=0; VAR=$(curl) || CURL_OK=$? (verified locally that the branch runs and the step exits 0, preserving the force_deploy override). Added --max-time/--retry to the hebcal curls.

CRITICAL fixed (freeze gate rewritten twice this cycle). Round 1 replaced a UTC-string-vs-offset-timestamp comparison (freeze opened for the first 2-3h of every Shabbat) and a dead holiday check; SKILL_HE.md was additionally still carrying the PRE-v1.3.0 fail-OPEN block, so the v1.3.0 fix had never reached Hebrew readers. Round 2, after Expert review, corrected a FALSE premise I had introduced: /shabbat DOES honour maj=on and returns holiday items INCLUDING erev entries (Erev Yom Kippur, Erev Rosh Hashana) that the /hebcal feed omits. My round-1 test had sampled a week with no major holiday and generalised from an empty result. Final design is a single /shabbat?M=on&maj=on feed with gy/gm/gd for today under TZ=Asia/Jerusalem, walking items in order, pairing each candle-lighting with the following havdalah, comparing epoch seconds.

CRITICAL fixed (found by Expert, not by my own tests): the loop overwrote START on every candles item, so a TWO-DAY yom tov (Rosh Hashana, or any chag adjacent to Shabbat) emits two candle-lightings before one havdalah and only the second night was tested. Deploys ran freely through the whole of Rosh Hashana day one AND erev Rosh Hashana. Fixed by keeping the EARLIEST unclosed candle-lighting. Test bank widened from 5 cases to 18 and now includes both RH days, erev-RH, YK erev/night/midday/after-havdalah, erev Sukkot, Sukkot I, chol between chagim, a winter date (UTC+2), hebcal-down, and a 200-with-empty-items shape guard. 18/18 pass. Root lesson: my first test bank spot-checked one holiday and one Shabbat; enumerating the holiday TYPES (one-day, two-day, chag-adjacent-to-Shabbat) was what actually found the bug.

CRITICAL fixed: command injection. ${{ }} is substituted as raw text before bash parses the line, so github.event.pull_request.title, github.head_ref/ref_name and workflow_dispatch override_reason were executing as code in jobs holding MONDAY_TOKEN, SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL and deploy tokens. All attacker-controlled context moved into env: blocks across SKILL.md, SKILL_HE.md, references/workflow-templates.md and references/shabbat-deploy-freeze.md; Slack payloads rebuilt with jq -n --arg so a quote or newline cannot break the JSON either. The skill had been TEACHING the safe pattern while modelling the unsafe one in the same file.

CRITICAL fixed (round 3, found by Expert): a ONE-DAY yom tov landing on a Friday (Shavuot 2027-06-11) left the gate OPEN all day. A feed requested for the chag itself starts that morning, so the previous evening's candle-lighting is outside its range, and the COMING Shabbat's candle-lighting shadowed the in-progress rescue. Added rule 1: freeze when any item carries `yomtov: true` dated today (Asia/Jerusalem), unless today's closing havdalah has already passed. `yomtov` is set on exactly the work-prohibited days and absent on chol hamoed, fasts and Shabbat Shuva, so it does not over-freeze. Test bank now enumerates holiday TYPES (one-day chag per weekday, two-day chag, chag adjacent to Shabbat, YK, Shmini Atzeret, chol hamoed, fasts, DST changeover weekends) rather than sampling dates; final review replayed the shipped bytes over 476 instants against an independently-derived ground truth with zero mismatches.

CRITICAL fixed (round 3): my own round-2 correction introduced two fail-opens in Template 1. `if: always()` re-enabled the deploy step when the GATE step crashed (no output written, so '' != 'true' passed), and the force_deploy escape I had just added was unreachable because the job was still gated on github.event_name == 'push'. Lesson: a fix to a safety gate needs the same adversarial trace as the original defect; 'always() so the override survives' sounded right and inverted the fail-closed property.

CRITICAL fixed: the canonical reference implementation, which both SKILL files tell the reader to use in production, failed OPEN on its holiday call (|| echo '{"items":[]}' makes an outage indistinguishable from 'no holiday today'). Now fails closed, and its date arithmetic runs under TZ=Asia/Jerusalem. Its DST rule was also still the pre-correction 'last Sunday BEFORE October'; corrected to 'last Sunday OF October' so all three files now agree.

Fixed: the frozen-deploy Slack message promised 'הפריסה תתבצע אוטומטית אחרי מוצאי שבת/חג' while nothing in the template queued anything; Template 1 also had no workflow_dispatch, so an hebcal outage hard-blocked production with no escape despite the fail-closed message telling the user to use force_deploy.
